newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks retreat early on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks retreat early on profit taking.

text.p: Singapore stocks retreated early on Tuesday, continuing the previous day's downtrend and profit taking linked to overnight falls in the Dow Jones.
"The market is featureless, mostly driven by events in Wall Street," a local bank dealer said, adding institutional demand for blue chip shares was weak.
The Straits Times Industrials Index eased 2.54 points to 2,035.335 at 0220 GMT on a turnover of 35.09 million shares.
Activity was mostly confined to over-the-counter issues and recent listings, which were supported by speculative interest amid a dearth of market moving factors.
Dealers said foreign institutions were sidelined on a perception that Asian stock markets were losing their lustre.
Top gainer SPH foreign rose Singapore 70 cents to S$27.00, merely recapturing the previous day's sharp losses.
OUB foreign and Creative Technology rose 30 and 20 cents to S$10.20 and S$19.70 respectively, also on a rebound.
Newly-listed MMI Holdings headed the actives list, down two cents to S$0.65, while property and consumer products firm KLI slipped seven cents to S$1.95.
L&M Group Investments stock was suspended on Tuesday pending an announcement.
